req.title: Login form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-007 requires GET /auth/login to return an HTTP 2xx response with a login form. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — standard GET returns 200 with form fields present; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST with no data) still serves the form but we also verify a truly wrong path returns 404; (3) boundary BVA — response body contains exactly the expected HTML landmarks (form action, input names) to catch mutations that change the template path or route prefix; (4) STC — unauthenticated vs authenticated state both reach the login page correctly; (5) DT — Content-Type header is text/html. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_login_get_returns_200
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database
actions: Send GET /auth/login with the Flask test client
expected: Response body contains the username input field
Response body contains the password input field
trace: R-FLASKR-007: GET /auth/login -> HTTP 2xx with login form payload
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_login_get_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data

test_login_get_returns_200()

tests.name: test_login_get_after_authenticated_session
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database with seed data
User Rahul (id=1, password=stone) exists in the database
actions: POST /auth/login with valid credentials to establish session
expected: Login form is still served (flaskr does not redirect logged-in users away)
trace: R-FLASKR-007: GET /auth/login must return 2xx regardless of session state
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_login_get_after_authenticated_session():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login',
        data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'},
        follow_redirects=False)
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'name="username"' in r.data
    assert b'name="password"' in r.data

test_login_get_after_authenticated_session()
